note: PR #65. A follow-on to error-channels (its own ledger is closed and covers a DIFFERENT cycle) — opened as a fix PR outside the roster, so this ledger is written retroactively at ship. Rounds 1-4 are recorded without per-round detail rather than reconstructed.

blocking: HIGH-1: stale base and, consequently, a stale golden. Everything else judged sound.

events.note: Rebased; golden regenerated BY MEASUREMENT with a control on main proving the procedure. Also fixed four comment defects, one of which -- 'the suite stayed 130/130' -- was a bare number with no harness, replaced by the mutation that reproduces the claim, RUN rather than asserted.

verified.golden: 23/809/5178 reproduced bit-for-bit from a clean build; producer sha256 374edd1c... on the branch vs 21859254... on main, both matching the implementer's claims to 64 hex digits -- so the producer really did rebuild
verified.B_vs_Wrap: derived from the code rather than from either framing: B is closed by the re-returning rhs (comes back as a DIRECT origin), Wrap survives TRANSITIVELY having never been covered. The replacement comment is true. I had previously given the peer a 'correction' that deleted the mechanism protecting Wrap.
verified.callgraph_diff_33: the symmetric 33-each-way movement is a SCRIPT ARTIFACT, proven by running the movement SQL between a database and a byte-identical copy of itself: nothing moved, it reported 33 each way. A control that cannot go green measures nothing.
verified.soundness: the arm-order blind spot is pre-existing and independent of or-patterns -- proven with a probe containing no or-pattern at all. This PR widens its syntactic scope by one form and pins that; it does not create it.

events.residual: MEDIUM-1: the flattener's RECURSION is untested -- every fixture was two-way, and only a three-way arm nests. Direction is safe (losing alternatives closes less), so precision not soundness.

events.note: Merged on a green CI run against the rebased head. The golden happened to equal main's value plus the claimed delta -- but it was MEASURED with a control, not computed, and that is the only reason the coincidence is evidence of anything.

items: tezt stops at the FIRST failing test, so both mutation runs left 26 of 144 tests unrun. 'Exactly one FAILURE' is literally true and narrower than it reads; the round-5 message's 'nothing else in the suite moves' is not established by that run.

scripts/callgraph-diff.sh's movement query reports phantom symmetric movements -- the join does not disambiguate duplicate (caller,callee,site) rows, and 21 homonym function names are a second source. Owned by the callgraph-diff script, documented not fixed.
Two stale figures survive in commit messages 3e3a7ce and 9c35470 ('130/130', '787/5070'). True when written, describing nothing reproducible now. Immutable history; not repeated.
